Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexWave Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexWave Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; David Kim, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Commercial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the Q3, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth.

Our achievements include robust EBITDA margin expansion to 38.5%, our strongest in three years, fueled by operational leverage, cost discipline, and a shift to high-margin services like premium 5G plans and fiber broadband. We are also seeing substantial growth from our 5G Standalone core rollout and fiber passings, with significant impacts on ARPU and subscriber retention. Further, we are concentrating on churn reduction to industry-leading levels through AI-driven interventions. Additionally, our network uptime and 5G coverage hitting 98% in North America is showing promise. We are also improving our spectral efficiency to 72% across our portfolio. We are strategically investing in Open RAN and edge computing for future-proofing. Finally, subscriber net adds exceeded 2 million, and we are exploring dividend increases alongside buybacks for shareholder value.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Alex. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $14.8 billion, representing a 7.2% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.7 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.5%, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 35.2% and 140 basis points sequentially from Q2's 37.1%. This puts us on track for a full-year 2024 EBITDA margin of 37.8%, surpassing our initial guidance of 36-37%.

Let me unpack the key drivers and trends behind this outperformance. Our margin expansion stems from operational leverage as capex intensity moderates after aggressive 5G and fiber buildouts. Wireless service revenue rose 8.1%, broadband 9.4%, while total opex as a percentage of revenue dropped 210 basis points to 61.5%. This success rests on cost discipline, a revenue mix shifting to high-margin services, and efficiencies from next-gen network investments.

In the wireless segment, comprising 52% of revenue, margins reached 42.7%, up from 39.8% year-over-year. ARPU expanded 4.2% to $58.30, propelled by our Unlimited Max 5G plan, now 62% of postpaid base, up from 48%. Postpaid phone net adds were 1.2 million, surpassing Verizon's figures, thanks to mid-band C-band deployment covering 85% of top 100 markets. Churn stayed at 0.76%, the industry's lowest, supported by our AI-powered retention platform using predictive analytics to target at-risk accounts 48 hours early.

Customer acquisition costs fell 15% year-over-year to $320 per gross add via digital marketing and Apple/Samsung trade-in partnerships. Interconnect and roaming expenses declined 8% as international traffic normalized. We absorbed $120 million in one-time 5G SA migration costs, impacting margins by 50 basis points, but those are now complete.

Broadband and wireline, 28% of revenue, saw margins climb to 35.2% from 32.1%, a 310 basis point gain. Fiber passings increased 12% to 45 million homes, take rates hit 52% on gigabit tiers at $95 monthly ARPU, akin to Comcast's model but with XGS-PON low latency. This mix shift contributed 180 basis points to margins.

Pole attachment and right-of-way fees rose 6% due to inflation, offset by 22% lower field service costs from our TeleMedia FieldOps AI optimizer, enhancing technician routing 30% via edge computing and drone inspections. Enterprise SD-WAN services grew 15%, boasting 55% margins.

Media and entertainment, 20% of revenue, achieved 28.4% margins, up from 25.6%. TeleStream+, our DTC platform, added 2.8 million subscribers to 28 million, ARPU at $13.50, narrowing the gap to Netflix via ad-supported tiers at 40% penetration. Ad revenue jumped 18% to $1.2 billion on connected TV trends like Roku's. We have 45 FAST channels integrated into LG and Vizio smart TVs.

Content amortization increased 11% to $2.1 billion from NBA rights renewals, but output deals with Warner Bros. Discovery cut original spend 14%, recovering 200 basis points. Affiliate fees grew 5%, countering 4% linear sub declines with hybrid bundles retaining 75% of cord-cutters.

Regionally, North America at 78% of EBITDA had 40.1% margins, leveraging AWS-3 spectrum advantages over AT&T and Canadian fiber like Bell Canada. Europe at 15% faced 32.8% margins from roaming caps and UK price controls, mitigated by Vodafone JV 5G FWA ramping to 1 million homes by year-end 2025. APAC/LatAm at 7% led with 45.2% margins from Brazil Oi integration and India 5G prepaid.

Year-to-date margins accelerated 300 basis points from Q1's 35.5%, outpacing T-Mobile. Our ORAN at 65% of RAN cut costs 18%, Cloud Native Core in 12 markets slashed opex 25%. AI Network Digital Twin predicts 95% outages, cutting MTTR 40%; GenAI chatbots handle 35% Tier 1 support; 5G NR LEDs reduced tower power 12%.

We're de-risking via capex re-phasing: FY24 at 16.5% of revenue or $8.9 billion, down from 19.2%. M&A like $2.5 billion Liberty Latin America stake targets 45% LatAm margins. We expect 100-200 basis point expansion in 2025 from FWA scale to 5 million subs and content efficiencies.

We continue to manage expenses prudently and optimize capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $2.8 billion this quarter, primarily for 5G and fiber, aligning with full-year guidance of $18.5 to $19.5 billion total, 80% or $15.0 to $15.6 billion for networks—a 3% midpoint increase from 2023's $14.8 billion, with intensity at 18-19% of service revenue.

Network capex breaks down as wireless $9.2 to $9.6 billion (62%), targeting 95% midband 5G North America coverage from 88%, with 25,000 Massive MIMO radios using Nokia/Samsung on 3.7 GHz C-band at $0.55 per MHz-POP. mmWave densification adds 8,000 small cells for 500,000 FWA subs by Q4. North America 70%, Europe JV $1.2 billion Open RAN, APAC $800 million sub-6 for IoT.

Wireline $3.5 to $3.7 billion (23%) for 12 million FTTH passings up 25%, $1.5 billion trenching with Corning, $500 million UK metro Ethernet. Media edge $2.3 billion (15%) for 5,000 CDN PoPs with Akamai, AWS Outposts, $400 million LatAm 5G sports streaming.

Investments are 55% H2-loaded, peaking 2025 at $16 billion before $14 billion by 2027 via vRAN 15-20% gains. 5G IRR over 25%, fiber payback under 5 years, edge 30% margins. $4 billion cash, A- rating mitigate supply risks.

Blended monthly churn was 1.18%, down 12% year-over-year from 1.34%, sequential 3% from 1.22%, annualizing to 13.8% below 18-20% industry. Postpaid mobility 0.85% (55% revenue, 28.5 million subs), down 15% YoY via 92% 5G SA top metros, family plans 42%. Fixed broadband 1.12% (14.2 million subs), 10% better on gigabit to 75%, though rural Starlink pressure. VeriStream+ 2.45% (22.8 million YTD adds), flat YoY, bundled at 1.65% vs. 3.2% standalone.

AI churn engine on 150 signals retained 68% of 1.2 million at-risk, 40 bps savings; 5G slicing cut stalls 22%. Price hikes added 5 bps drag, T-Mobile FWA 2-3% share loss. NFL deals, originals like Echoes of Tomorrow boosted sessions 15%.

North America 1.15% U.S., 1.35% Canada; Europe 1.32% JV; LatAm 1.65% Brazil. FY24 guide 1.15-1.20%, targeting sub-1.0% FY26 via GenAI, 60% 3-play bundles, $1.5 billion Open RAN/6G.

David Kim: Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage and increasing network capacity. In Q3, 5G capex was $1.82 billion of $2.8 billion total, 70% of core modernization, up 12% year-over-year to support media data at 42% ARPU uplift.

Sub-6GHz covers 98% North America (280 million people), C-band live 85% top 100 U.S. markets from $3.2 billion Auction 107. mmWave to 45 metros, 1.8 Gbps peaks, #1 Ookla. 5G SA 25% sites from 8%, Ericsson dual-mode for URLLC; 14 enterprise deals, Hollywood AR/VR under 5ms.

Open RAN 15% new rural, Nokia/Rakuten for 20-25% backhaul savings. U.S. $1.1 billion media hubs; Europe $220 million Vodafone JV 92% coverage, cloud gaming; APAC $180 million IndiWave FWA 85% take rates.

5G subs 62%, ARPU +7% QoQ to $58.40 on NFL streams. $450 million opex savings YTD vRAN/AI. Q4 5G capex $1.4 billion, FY intensity 26-27% tapering 24% 2025.

We're also investing in advanced technologies like network slicing and edge computing to support new applications and services. Our network uptime and reliability remain high. We are also improving spectral efficiency through Dynamic Spectrum Sharing.

On spectrum assets, utilization is 72% network-wide, up from 58%, on 240 MHz mid-band: 160 MHz C-band $0.45/MHz-POP, 60 MHz 2.5 GHz, 20 MHz CBRS; 80 MHz 600 MHz, 120 MHz mmWave 35 DMAs.

Low-band 65% for FWA 1.2 million $25 ARPU; mid-band 82% urban 450 Mbps, video 45%, MEC 18%; mmWave 48% AR/VR. Northeast 88%, Sun Belt 75%, Midwest 55%. DSS +22% efficiency.

Future: refarm 3G AWS-3 to 5G by 2025 +15% capacity; $800 million C-band SA to 3 million FWA, 95% clearance; CBRS 20 MHz 500 sites for private 5G media/smart cities; mmWave sharing, Auction 108 100 MHz $0.35/MHz-POP. 30% new capacity content slices sub-10ms 8K.

$1.2 billion spectrum opex, 3.5x ROI 18% ARPU lift, 12-15% wireless EBITDA CAGR.

Lisa Chen: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth and improved customer satisfaction scores this quarter. Our bundled service offerings are resonating well with customers, and we're focused on providing a seamless and personalized customer experience. We are also focused on increasing broadband and streaming attach rates through exclusive content and 5G convergence.

Raj Patel: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to enhance our network and services. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations and improve efficiency, including GenAI for support and digital twins. We are also working on developing new products and services that leverage 5G and edge computing. Our R&D efforts are concentrated on ORAN virtualization, 5G-Advanced, and low-latency media processing.

Maria Gonzalez: To wrap our prepared remarks, let me provide guidance on subscriber and revenue growth, plus shareholder returns. Total subscribers hit 148.7 million Q3; Q4 to 152.3 million, +2.4% sequential, 7.8% YoY. Wireless 112.4 million +1.8% QoQ, 2.3 million adds (postpaid phone 1.4 million, prepaid 900K); broadband 28.1 million +5.2%, 1.1 million (FWA 750K); video 11.8 million +3.1%, 360K.

FY25 162.5 million, +9.2%. Q4 revenue $15.6 billion +5.4% QoQ, 8.1% YoY, service +6.2%; wireless service $10.2 billion +6.8%, ARPU $52.40 +2.1%; broadband $2.9 billion +11.2%; media $1.4 billion +7.5%. FY25 $64.2 billion +11.5%, EBITDA margin 48.2% +150 bps.

North America 92% growth, EMEA 4%, LatAm 15%. Private 5G stadiums, edge AI NexusStream -40% buffering, $500M content.

On dividends, quarterly $0.55/share ($2.20 annual), 4.8% yield at $45.75. 18th year increases, 5-year CAGR 4.2%. Q3 FCF $1.8 billion +12% YoY, TTM $6.2 billion post-$4.1 billion capex. FCF payout 35% <45-50%; EPS 58%, 2.1x GAAP; EBITDA-FCF 92%.

FY24 FCF $6.5-7.0 billion supports 5% raise to $0.5775 Q1 2025 ($2.31, 5.0-5.5% yield). Leverage 2.3x, $3.1B cash. YTD returns $4.8 billion ($3.2B dividends, $1.6B buybacks under $5B auth), $10.45/share 22% cap. 70/30 dividend-buyback.

North America FWA 450K adds 15% FCF margin; Europe bundling 92.6% retention; APAC Indonesia 1.2M 5G $8.50 ARPU. ORAN 40% RAN -15% capex; TeleStream 18M subs $450M EBITDA; tuck-ins; 25% renewables.

FY25-26 $7-8B FCF enables $5B+ returns, 6-7% yield.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Jack Thompson with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Jack Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding spectrum allocation for private networks and slicing?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Jack. We're aggressively targeting enterprises with our CBRS and mid-band assets, allocating 20 MHz PALs to over 500 sites via SAS with Google and Federated Wireless. This enables slicable private 5G for media production like live sports AR and smart cities, competing via Open RAN cost savings and low-latency under 5ms from 5G SA. We've signed 14 deals including Hollywood studios for AR/VR, mirroring Mandalorian tech, while mmWave sharing with cable peers cuts densification costs. Our 3.5 GHz Auction 108 pursuit adds 100 MHz at low cost, positioning us ahead of Cisco Viptela in SD-WAN with 55% margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding capex re-phasing and FCF generation?

Maria Gonzalez: Great question, Emily. Inflation at 3.2% CPI hit pole fees 6%, but AI FieldOps cut services 22%, ORAN vendor costs 18%, vRAN opex 25%. Rising rates are managed with A- rating, $4B cash, 2.3x leverage; green bonds at 75bps for renewables. Capex FY24 $8.9B 16.5% revenue down from 19.2%, FY25 peak $16B then taper via efficiencies. FCF TTM $6.2B supports 35% payout, FY24 $6.5-7B funds dividend raise and buybacks, with EchoFiber synergies $2.5B offsetting. Regional hedges like LatAm Oi integration yield 45% margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from Michael Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Michael Lee: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing energy efficiency in 5G deployments and ESG-linked returns?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Michael. Sustainability is core; 5G NR LEDs dropped tower power 12% at $0.15/kWh U.S. averages, targeting 25% renewables by YE24 for green bonds lowering WACC to 6.2%. Network Digital Twin preempts 95% outages, MTTR -40%; edge computing optimizes routing. Success via FCF acceleration—ORAN/6G $1.5B 2025 cuts emissions while driving 15% opex savings. ROI tracks 25%+ IRR on 5G, fiber <5 years payback, aligning shareholder value with ESG metrics like 92% EBITDA-FCF conversion.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in NexWave Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
